solution.what: Web search for KAA 4591 and Augurelio ciphers
DECODE record list from the API dump (141 records in the volume); images of the 14 targets and 30 neighbouring keys fetched with the cookie
R9423 key-register block 2_4 (Hz. Wilhelm) applied to R9367
Annealing with nulls allowed on R9367 (de-1500s, homophone caps): failed
R9423 block 2_4 read at zoom (keys9423/2_4_zoom.txt) and the frequent signs re-matched by shape: the key fits; ⊡ ≈ ♀ are nulls/dividers; five values added from context; reading in r9367/reading.txt

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from kaa4591 (catalogue 161), whose fourteen records are letters in at least six systems: System A′ stays in kaa4591; Łaski's System B is kaa4591b; R9325 is fulda1576; R9367, R9416, R9424 and R9319 are r9367, r9416, r9424 and r9319; R9291 is a key fragment. Words of the decoded runs counted with measure.py.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): r9367/transcription.txt + signs.txt, the rough reading r9367/reading.txt (unread signs marked); key copied from NOTES.md and the reading header to texts/key.md, with r9367/key_match.md

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). r9367/reading.txt read line by line: the cipher runs carry unread signs mid-word in most lines ('{s w a r d e [#] i n l?}', '{sa ber vir bar niwt [#] ...}'); only a few phrases assemble (docs/_check_reading.py: 14 of 35 sentences clean, mostly the clear German). Relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved (key kept as a part); fraction_read 0.545 -> 0.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, batch b32): DECODE R9367 fetched logged in (2 images, no attachment); P2 opened for the first time: the blank back with two pen crosses, no address. Neighbours R9366 (key) and R9368 (Augurelio letter, other cipher) checked: no decipherment of f. 169.

P1 rotated and read at full resolution in tiles: every cipher run re-transcribed (r9367/transcription_v2.txt, R9367_corrections.tsv: ‡‡ vs cc, boxed H vs boxed dot, new S and d labels, π at L32) and the clear German re-read.

Values that hold at every occurrence adopted: v = b/w, ‡‡ = u (guet, verkhuntschaft, und, hindurch, vergunt, euch), boxed H = k; sense-only, flagged: cc = z (zeit, ziechen, Schmalcz, selczam, herczen), Φ = b (bin, bringen, botschaft, bring), S = sch (verkhuntschaft, botschaft, Schmalcz), U = ll (alles). # and Π stay unidentified.

r9367/R9367_reading.md and _en.md built line by line; every cipher word aligned with the decode (research/reading_audit/b32_r9367_dec.py); score 0.641 (25/39) on explicit holes with code signs counted as holes, 0.256 plain; look-alike letters ~2/470. Relabelled read (grade B).

Verify sweep (reading audit v2): R9367 reading re-scored with the 11 words that rest on the sense-only values cc = z, Φ = b, S = sch, U = ll counted as holes (and the unread signs [#], [Π], [R], [g] as holes): explicit-hole share 0.641 -> 0.590 (23/39), b17 HOLES=1 0.667; plain 0.231. The cipher passages L09-10, L14, L16, L31, L34 do not build sentences. DECODE image re-fetched and viewed; the failures are key values, not transcription. Demoted to decoded, not read; class not read, fraction_read 0.

Method restored: key obtained by block 2_4 of the key register R9423 in the same volume, extended from the letter's own words (read with known key); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

Method restored 24 Oct 2026 (George Lasry: a key can be mostly recovered while the text is not read): the key was obtained by block 2_4 of the key register R9423 in the same volume, extended from the letter's own words; class stays not read, as the text does not read.

texts.label: KAA 4591 f. 169, 22 March 1535
texts.summary: A son to his father, Monday after Palm Sunday 1535, in German with cipher passages: he was questioned about strange arts and denied everything, claiming to be a poor writer sent to learn because he is young; he has not yet learnt anything thorough and will report when he reaches the place; he will bring his body through; someone asked how 'he' brings [a person, code sign] the message; many Turks are moving up. Postscript: Friedrich Schmalcz begrudges the father nothing good. Cipher runs in key R9423 block 2_4, extended.
texts.note: Verify sweep 23 Oct 2026 (reading audit v2): back to decoded, not read. The b32 reading (r9367/R9367_reading.md, kept as a partial reading) scored 0.641 (25/39) on explicit holes with four key values that rest on sense alone (cc = z: zeit, ziechen, Schmalcz, selczam, herczen; Φ = b: bin, bringen, botschaft, bring; S = sch: verkhuntschaft, botschaft, Schmalcz; U = ll: alles). Counting those 11 words as holes gives 0.590 (23/39; 0.231 plain, the 1535 spelling), under the bar, and the cipher passages L09-10 ('die [#] fleih danck geben worden'), L14 ('kaub sains gehalten'), L16, L31 ('ich trag ssorg [R] hab sich merers vermessen s weder er') and L34 do not build sentences. Image IMG_R9367_I44333_P1 re-fetched and viewed: the failures are key values, not shapes. Blocker: no-key-material (# 13x, Π 4x, R, d and the four values are not in register block 2_4; no second letter or decipherment in this key).
